Hi Laurent / Sophie — thanks again for your time on the demo this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can get legal/compliance moving: 

Call recap (short):
- Use case: customer support triage + routing (no payment data in RL, some policy-flagged PII).
- Expected traffic: ~3M tokens/month initially; spiky during incident periods.

Compliance asks we discussed:
1) SOC 2 status — you flagged needing an in-scope SOC 2 report and an executive summary.
2) GDPR: DPA execution and SCC module selection (you mentioned wanting clarity on controller vs processor).
3) Vendor security questionnaire — we should kick that off (I'll send a short checklist).

Immediate next steps I propose:
- I'll share our DPA template and a condensed SOC 2 summary now (see attachments).
- Recommend SCC Module: initial recommendation is Module 2 (Processor as a Service) but want to confirm your perspective on any joint-controller activities (e.g., deriving metrics from customer text).
- If you confirm Module 2 and that Redwood acts as processor, we can send the DPA via DocuSign and your legal team can review redlines.

Can you confirm: (a) that Insura wants Redwood to act as processor only, (b) whether you require joint-controller clauses for analytics, and (c) a target date for DPA completion?

I attached: Redwood_DPA_Template_v2.pdf and a one-page SOC2 summary (SOC2_Report_Redwood_2026-summary.pdf).

Thanks — I can jump on a short call tomorrow with legal if helpful.

Best,

Thanks Karthik — appreciated the recap. A couple quick clarifications from our security and legal teams before we route internally: 

- Controller vs Processor: our default is to treat service providers as processors. The only reason we'd consider joint-controller language is if Redwood is expected to build derived insights that Insura plans to publish externally (analytics that identify market trends). At present that is not in scope. So lean processor-only.

- SOC 2: the summary looks useful. Can you confirm whether the full SOC 2 report is available under NDA or if there is a public attestation PDF? Our compliance team prefers a full Type II report or at least an auditor-signed attestation.

- SCC module: we saw your suggestion of Module 2. Can you state which controller/processor options map to Module 2 in your DPA and what changes if we requested Module 1 (controller-centric)?

I'll loop Sophie who owns procurement for timing.

Laurent — thanks, good to know that analytics publishing is out of scope for now. Quick answers below and a next-step proposal: 

1) Processor stance: Redwood will act as Processor. We do not assert controller rights over customer content. Our DPA template has the processor module selected by default; that maps to SCC Module 2 in the SCC wording. If you prefer Module 1, we'd need to discuss which processing activities you'd like Redwood to control (that will change liability and some obligations).

2) SOC 2: The full Type II report is available to customers under NDA. I've attached the 1-page signed SOC 2 summary for quick review; if you want the full auditor report we can execute an NDA and provide the full PDF within 24–48 hours.

3) SCC mapping: short mapping: 
- DPA with Processor module -> SCC Module 2 (Processor as Service).
- DPA with Joint-controller clauses or explicit rights over derived analytics -> SCC Module 1 or bespoke mapping.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm processor-only (sounds like yes) and we’ll send the DPA via DocuSign with Module 2 pre-selected.
- We can execute an NDA and drop the full SOC 2 Type II report in your secure bucket (or provide a one-time access link).
- I'll open a security questionnaire in our portal and send an invite to your security team (Soojin from Redwood will help coordinate).

If that's green, I'll prepare the DocuSign envelope (DPA + Module 2) and set a tentative target of signing by 2027-04-20 to keep your launch timeline intact.

Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
